questions.prompt: Block $A$ is traveling with a speed $v_0$ on a smooth surface when the surface suddenly becomes rough with a coefficient of friction $\mu$, causing the block to stop after a distance $d$. If block $A$ were traveling twice as fast ($2v_0$), how far would it travel on the rough surface before stopping?
questions.solution: Work and energy: $T_1 + U_{1\to2} = T_2$ gives $\tfrac12 m v_0^2 - \mu m g\,d = 0$, so $d = \dfrac{v_0^2}{2\mu g}$. The stopping distance is proportional to $v_0^2$: doubling the speed multiplies the kinetic energy (and hence the distance) by $4$, giving $4d$.

questions.prompt: A $400\text{-kg}$ satellite was placed in a circular orbit $1500\,\text{km}$ above the surface of the earth, where the acceleration of gravity is $6.43\,\text{m/s}^2$. Knowing that its orbital speed is $25.6\times10^3\,\text{km/h}$, determine the kinetic energy of the satellite (in GJ).
questions.solution:
The mass is $400\,\text{kg}$ regardless of the local $g$. $v = 25.6\times10^6\,\text{m}/3600\,\text{s} = 7111\,\text{m/s}$.

$$T = \tfrac12 mv^2 = \tfrac12(400)(7111)^2 = 10.11\times10^9\,\text{J} = 10.11\,\text{GJ}.$$

questions.prompt: A $1\text{-lb}$ stone is dropped down a hole on the moon ($g_{\text{moon}} = 5.31\,\text{ft/s}^2$) and strikes the bottom with a speed of $95\,\text{ft/s}$. Neglecting air resistance, determine the height $h$ from which it was dropped (in ft). (The stone's mass is that of a stone weighing $1\,\text{lb}$ on earth.)
questions.solution:
$m = 1/32.2\,\text{lb}\cdot\text{s}^2/\text{ft}$, so $T_2 = \tfrac12(1/32.2)(95)^2 = 140.1\,\text{ft}\cdot\text{lb}$. On the moon the stone's weight is $mg_{\text{moon}}$, and $T_1 + U_{1\to2} = T_2$ gives $0 + m g_{\text{moon}} h = \tfrac12 m v^2$:

$$h = \frac{v^2}{2g_{\text{moon}}} = \frac{95^2}{2(5.31)} = 850\,\text{ft}.$$

questions.prompt: Packages are thrown down a $30^\circ$ incline at $A$ with a velocity of $1\,\text{m/s}$ and slide along the surface $ABC$ (incline $AB$ of length $d$, then horizontal $BC = 7\,\text{m}$) to a conveyor belt. Knowing that $\mu_k = 0.25$ between the packages and the surface, determine the distance $d$ (in m) if the packages are to arrive at $C$ with a velocity of $2\,\text{m/s}$.

A $1200\text{-kg}$ trailer is hitched to a $1400\text{-kg}$ car. The car and trailer are traveling at $72\,\text{km/h}$ when the driver applies the brakes on both. Knowing that the braking forces exerted on the car and the trailer are $5000\,\text{N}$ and $4000\,\text{N}$, respectively, determine the distance traveled before they come to a stop (in m).
questions.solution:
Treat car + trailer as one system (the hitch forces cancel). $v_1 = 72\,\text{km/h} = 20\,\text{m/s}$, $T_1 = \tfrac12(2600)(20)^2 = 520\,000\,\text{J}$, $T_2 = 0$.

$$T_1 + U_{1\to2} = T_2: \quad 520\,000 - (5000 + 4000)x = 0 \implies x = 57.8\,\text{m}.$$

(For the car alone: $280\,000 - 5000(57.8) + H(57.8) = 0$ gives a hitch force $H = 154\,\text{N}$.)

questions.prompt: Using $g_h = g_0R^2/(R+h)^2$ with $R = 6370\,\text{km}$, determine the percent error if the weight that an object has on the surface of the earth is used as its weight at an altitude of $1000\,\text{km}$.
questions.solution:
$$\frac{g_h}{g_0} = \left(\frac{6370}{6370 + 1000}\right)^2 = (0.8643)^2 = 0.7470.$$

The true weight is $0.747$ of the surface weight, so using the surface weight overestimates by $1 - 0.747 = 0.253$ of the surface weight: error $= 25.3\%$.

questions.prompt: The frictional resistance of a ship varies directly as the $1.75$ power of its speed. A single tugboat at full power tows the ship at $4.5\,\text{km/h}$ by exerting a constant force of $300\,\text{kN}$. Determine the maximum speed (in km/h) at which two tugboats, each capable of delivering the same power, can tow the ship.
questions.solution:
One tug: $P = Fv = (300\,\text{kN})(1.25\,\text{m/s}) = 375\,\text{kW}$. With $F = Kv^{1.75}$, the towing power is $P = Fv = Kv^{2.75}$. Doubling the power:

$$\left(\frac{v_2}{v_1}\right)^{2.75} = 2 \implies v_2 = 4.5(2)^{1/2.75} = 4.5(1.2867) = 5.79\,\text{km/h}.$$

questions.prompt: The sphere at $A$ (level with $O$) is given a downward velocity $v_0$ and swings in a vertical circle of radius $l$ about $O$. If $AO$ is a **rope**, what is the smallest $v_0$ for which the sphere reaches point $B$ directly above $O$?
questions.solution: At $B$ a rope can only pull, so $T \ge 0$; with $T = 0$, $\sum F_n = ma_n$ gives $mg = mv_B^2/l$, i.e. $v_B^2 = gl$. Conservation of energy from $A$ to $B$ (rise $l$): $\tfrac12 mv_0^2 = \tfrac12 mv_B^2 + mgl \implies v_0^2 = gl + 2gl = 3gl$, so $v_0 = \sqrt{3gl}$. ($\sqrt{2gl}$ is the answer for a massless **rod**, which can have $v_B = 0$.)

questions.prompt: The sphere at $A$ is given a downward velocity $v_0 = 5\,\text{m/s}$ and swings in a vertical plane at the end of a rope of length $l = 2\,\text{m}$ attached to a support at $O$ ($OA$ horizontal). Determine the angle $\theta$ (below the horizontal, in degrees) at which the rope will break, knowing that it can withstand a maximum tension equal to twice the weight of the sphere.
questions.solution:
Energy from $A$ to the position at angle $\theta$ (drop $l\sin\theta$): $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2gl\sin\theta = 25 + 39.24\sin\theta$.

Normal direction (toward $O$): $T - mg\sin\theta = mv^2/l$. With $T = 2mg$:

$$2(9.81) - 9.81\sin\theta = \frac{25 + 39.24\sin\theta}{2} \implies 7.12 = 29.43\sin\theta$$

$\sin\theta = 0.2419$, $\theta = 14.0^\circ$.

questions.prompt: An elastic bungee cable for a $130\text{-ft}$ tower is $85\,\text{ft}$ long unstretched and has spring constant $k = 533.3\,\text{lb/ft}$ (chosen so that a $600\text{-lb}$ weight dropped from the tower stretches it to $100\,\text{ft}$). How close to the ground (in ft) will a $186\text{-lb}$ man come if he uses this cable to jump from the tower?
questions.solution:
Check $k$: $600(100) = \tfrac12 k(15)^2 \Rightarrow k = 533.3\,\text{lb/ft}$. For the man, with stretch $x$ at the lowest point ($T_1 = T_2 = 0$):

$$186(85 + x) = \tfrac12(533.3)x^2 \implies 266.7x^2 - 186x - 15\,810 = 0$$

$x = 8.06\,\text{ft}$, so the lowest point is $85 + 8.06 = 93.06\,\text{ft}$ below the top: clearance $= 130 - 93.06 = 37.0\,\text{ft}$.

questions.prompt: A spring ($k = 30\,\text{kN/m}$, initially compressed $50\,\text{mm}$ by cables) is used to stop a $50\text{-kg}$ package moving down a $20^\circ$ incline. The package has a velocity of $2\,\text{m/s}$ when it is $8\,\text{m}$ from the spring, and $\mu_k = 0.2$ between package and incline. Determine the maximum additional deformation of the spring (in m).

A $35\,000\text{-Mg}$ ocean liner has an initial velocity of $4\,\text{km/h}$. Neglecting the frictional resistance of the water, determine the time (in s) required to bring the liner to rest using a single tugboat which exerts a constant force of $150\,\text{kN}$.

A $2500\text{-lb}$ automobile is moving at a speed of $60\,\text{mi/h}$ when the brakes are fully applied, causing all four wheels to skid. Determine the time (in s) required to stop the automobile on an icy road ($\mu_k = 0.10$).
questions.solution:
$v_1 = 88\,\text{ft/s}$; friction $F = \mu_k W$. Impulse and momentum: $\dfrac{W}{g}v_1 - \mu_k W t = 0$, so

$$t = \frac{v_1}{\mu_k g} = \frac{88}{0.10(32.2)} = 27.3\,\text{s}.$$

(On dry pavement, $\mu_k = 0.75$ gives $3.64\,\text{s}$.)

questions.prompt: In the hop of a triple jump, an athlete approaches with a horizontal velocity of $10\,\text{m/s}$, remains in contact with the ground for $0.18\,\text{s}$, and takes off at $50^\circ$ with a velocity of $12\,\text{m/s}$. The vertical component of the average impulsive force exerted by the ground on his foot is closest to:
questions.solution:
Vertical impulse and momentum (the weight acts throughout the $0.18\,\text{s}$ and must be included): $0 + (F_y - W)(0.18) = \dfrac{W}{g}(12\sin 50^\circ)$.

$$F_y = W\left[1 + \frac{9.193}{9.81(0.18)}\right] = W(1 + 5.21) = 6.21W.$$

Option A forgets the weight's impulse.

questions.prompt: The velocity of an $80\text{-kg}$ athlete just before landing in a sand pit is $9\,\text{m/s}$ at an angle of $35^\circ$ with the horizontal, and he comes to a complete stop $0.22\,\text{s}$ after landing. Determine the horizontal component of the average impulsive force exerted on his feet (in kN).

A $1.62\text{-oz}$ golf ball is hit with a club and leaves it with a velocity of $100\,\text{mi/h}$. For $0 \le t \le t_0$ the force on the ball is $F = F_m\sin(\pi t/t_0)$, with $t_0 = 0.5\,\text{ms}$. Determine $F_m$ (in lb).
questions.solution:
Impulse: $\int_0^{t_0} F_m\sin(\pi t/t_0)\,dt = \dfrac{2F_m t_0}{\pi}$. Momentum: $m = (1.62/16)/32.2 = 0.003144\,\text{lb}\cdot\text{s}^2/\text{ft}$, $v = 146.67\,\text{ft/s}$, $mv = 0.4612\,\text{lb}\cdot\text{s}$ (weight nonimpulsive).

$$F_m = \frac{\pi(0.4612)}{2(0.0005)} = 1449\,\text{lb} = 1.449\,\text{kips}.$$

questions.prompt: Tennis balls dropped onto a rigid surface from a height of $100\,\text{in.}$ must bounce to a height $53\,\text{in.} \le h \le 58\,\text{in.}$ The corresponding range of the coefficient of restitution is:
questions.solution: Fall: $v = \sqrt{2g(100)}$. Rigid surface: $v' = ev$. Rebound height $h = v'^2/2g = e^2(100)$, so $e = \sqrt{h/100}$: $\sqrt{0.53} = 0.728$ to $\sqrt{0.58} = 0.762$. Option A forgets that $h$ varies as $e^2$.

questions.prompt: Two disks sliding on a frictionless horizontal plane with opposite velocities of the same magnitude $v_0$ hit each other squarely. Disk $A$ weighs $6\,\text{lb}$ and is observed to have zero velocity after impact. Knowing that the coefficient of restitution between the disks is $0.5$, determine the weight of disk $B$ (in lb).
questions.solution:
Positive in the direction of $A$'s motion: $v_A = v_0$, $v_B = -v_0$, $v'_A = 0$.

Restitution: $v'_B - 0 = e[v_0 - (-v_0)] = 2(0.5)v_0 = v_0$.

Momentum: $m_A v_0 - m_B v_0 = m_B(v_0) \implies m_A = 2m_B$, so $W_B = 6/2 = 3.00\,\text{lb}$.
